source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And the worldly [or: common, unlearned] people and sinners were approaching him so that they might hear him

translation_notes: בעבור (עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because the clause שישמעוהו ('that they would hear him') follows, indicating purpose.
textual_notes: עולמיים is unusual — it could mean 'worldly people' (from עולם, 'world/age') or possibly 'people of the nations/common folk'. The form with double yod suggests an adjectival plural 'worldly ones'.

verses.literal: And they were drawing-near to him worldly-ones and sinners in-order-that they-would-hear-him

verses.translation: And the scribes and the Pharisees [separated ones] were grumbling, saying: Look, this one receives sinners and eats with them

translation_notes: ראה (first instance): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh (name)'. Chose H7200 as imperative 'see!/look!' — fits as an exclamatory introduction to the complaint.

זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 because it functions as a demonstrative pronoun pointing to the person being complained about. H2089 'sheep' would be incoherent here.

ראה (second instance): Candidates same as above. Chose H7200 in the sense of 'receives/welcomes' (figurative use of 'seeing' = accepting, cf. Hebrew usage where ראה can mean to regard favorably or receive). Context: the scribes complain he receives sinners and eats with them.
ואכל: Candidates: H398 'to eat', H399 'to eat', H400 'food', H401 'Ucal (name)'. Chose H398 because the verb 'eats' fits the complaint about table fellowship with sinners.
textual_notes: The second ראה is ambiguous — it could be parsed as another imperative 'see!' (making it 'See! This one! See sinners! And eats with them') or as a finite verb 'he sees/receives sinners'. The latter reading ('receives sinners') produces a more coherent complaint. Some Hebrew texts use ראה in the sense of 'accept/welcome'—this may be a Hebraism for 'receives'.

verses.literal: And the scribes and the separated-ones murmuring saying see this-one receives sinners and eats with-them

verses.translation: And he said to them this parable [or: word, matter]: And the steward said within himself, What shall I do, since my master is taking from me my stewardship? I do not know [how] to dig; I have shame to beg.

translation_notes: והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — pronoun 'he' fits as subject of 'said'.

אמר (both instances): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 — verb 'said' fits both narrative contexts.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative introducing the parable.

הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 — 'the word/matter' fits as introduction to a parable. H1907 'vizier' would be odd as it has the article prefix already embedded.
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 same. Chose H4100 — interrogative 'what' in the steward's internal question.

בושת: The root שת candidates: H8351 'tumult', H8352 'Sheth (name)', H8353 'six'. But בושת as a whole word means 'shame' (from בוש 'to be ashamed' + feminine ending). Chose to read as 'shame' which fits the context of the steward's embarrassment.

לשאול: Candidates: H7585 'Sheol/underworld', H7586 'Shaul (name)', H193 'body/powerful'. The consonants שאל mean 'to ask/beg'. In context the steward says he is ashamed to beg, which is coherent. H7585 'Sheol' would produce nonsense here.
textual_notes: והמורשה (H4181 'possession') is being used here in the sense of 'steward' — one entrusted with a possession/estate. This is a semantic extension: the one who manages the מורשה.
הרשאתי appears to be a late/post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'my authorization/stewardship' — not found in classical Strong's entries.
לשאול could theoretically be 'to Sheol' (H7585) but contextually 'to beg/ask' (from שאל) is clearly intended.

verses.literal: And he said to-them this [is] the word and the steward said in-his-heart what shall-I-do that my-master takes from-me my-authorization I-am-not knowing to-dig shame there-is to-me to-ask

verses.translation: Which [one] among you who has a hundred sheep [flock], and one of them is lost — will he not leave the ninety-nine in the open field [wilderness] and go after the one that was lost until he finds it? I do not know what I shall do when I am removed from the stewardship, in such a way that they will receive me into [their] house.

translation_notes: אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/which?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 — interrogative 'which?' introducing a rhetorical question about who among them.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this or that'. Chose H2088 — combined with אי forms 'which one' (אי זה = which).
שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble', H3426 'there is'. Chose H3426 — ש is relative particle + יש 'there is', meaning 'who has'. Marble makes no sense here.
מאה: Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah (tower)', H3969 'a hundred'. Chose H3967 — numeral 'a hundred' sheep.
מהם: The ם suffix is 'them'; candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'from them' referring to the flock.
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not'. Chose H3808 — rhetorical negative question 'will he not leave?'
במדבר: Candidates: H4057 'wilderness/open pasture', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H4057 — the open field where sheep graze.
שאבד: Candidates: H6 'to wander away/be lost/perish', H7 same (Aramaic), H8 'destruction'. Chose H6 — 'that was lost' fits the lost sheep narrative.
עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same, H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 — temporal 'until' before finding the sheep.
מה: Candidates: H4100/H4101 'what?'. Chose H4100.
מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 — preposition 'from' the stewardship.
באופן: H212 'a wheel'. Here used in post-biblical Hebrew sense of 'in a manner/way' (באופן ש = 'so that'). The word אופן evolved from 'wheel' to 'manner/way'.
בבית: Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 — 'into a house' meaning into their homes.
textual_notes: This section appears to interleave two narratives: the parable of the lost sheep (אי זה מכם...עד שימצאה) and the steward's soliloquy (איני יודע מה אעשה...). The transition is abrupt, suggesting either a scribal conflation or an intentional interweaving. The steward's speech from section 3 continues here.
באופן (H212 'wheel') is used in its post-biblical Hebrew semantic development meaning 'manner/way'. This suggests the text is from a later period of Hebrew.
מסולק is a post-biblical/rabbinic Hebrew form meaning 'removed/dismissed' — not found in classical biblical Hebrew.

verses.literal: Which this from-you that there-is to-him a-hundred flock and-is-lost one from-them not will-he-leave ninety and-nine in-the-wilderness and-will-go to-that-one that-was-lost until he-finds-her I-am-not knowing what I-shall-do when-I-will-be removed from the-authorization in-such-a-way that-they-will-receive-me in-a-house

verses.translation: And when he finds it, he places it upon his shoulders. He called [them] one by one, from among his master's debtors, and said to the first: How much are you indebted to my master?

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — כאשר = 'when/as', temporal conjunction.

ישימה: H3451 'desolation' is the dictionary entry for this form, but contextually this is clearly the verb שים 'to place/put' + 3fs suffix הּ ('her/it'). The verb ישים means 'he will place' and the suffix refers to the sheep. H3451 'desolation' makes no sense here.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 — preposition 'upon' his shoulders.
קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call (Aramaic)', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 — 'he called' the debtors.
אחד אחד: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 for both — distributive 'one by one' (each one individually).
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-564 various. Chose H559 — 'and he said'.
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what?/how?'. Chose H4100 — כ + מה = 'how much?' (interrogative about the amount of debt).
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 — pronoun 'you' as subject of the question.
textual_notes: This section again interleaves two narratives: the shepherd placing the sheep on his shoulders (from the lost sheep parable) and the steward calling debtors (from the steward parable). The transition between the two happens mid-verse without explicit marker.
ישימה: The Strong's entry H3451 'desolation' shares these consonants but is clearly not the intended reading. This is the imperfect of שים 'to set/place' with 3fs object suffix.

verses.literal: And when he-finds her he-places-her upon his-shoulders he-called one one from-the-debtors-of his-master and-said to-the-first how-much you [are] obligated to-my-master

verses.translation: And he came to his house rejoicing, calling [together] his friends and his neighbors, and said: Rejoice with me, for I have found the sheep [flock] that was lost! And he answered him: A hundred measures of oil. And he said to him: Take your bill [document], and do [it] quickly, and write fifty.

translation_notes: אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H409 same, H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'to/near/among'. Chose H413 — preposition 'to' his house.
שמח: Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up/be glad', H8056 'blithe/gleeful', H4220 'fat/rich', H4221 'marrow'. Chose H8056 — adjective 'rejoicing/glad' describing how he came home.
קורא: H6981 'Kore (name)'. However, this is clearly the active participle of קרא (H7121) 'calling'. The form קורא = 'one who calls'. Used here as participle.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for/that'. Chose H3588 — causal conjunction 'for/because'.
מאה: Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah (tower)', H3969 'a hundred'. Chose H3967.
שמן: Candidates: H8080 'to be oily', H8081 'oil/grease', H8082 'greasy/rich', H4478-4482 various מן readings. Chose H8081 — 'oil' as the commodity owed.
והוא (both): Chose H1931 'he' — pronoun identifying the speakers in dialogue.
אמר (both): Chose H559 'to say'.
ועשה: H6213 'to do/make'. Imperative 'do [it]'.
מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'promptly/quickly', H2029 'to conceive', H2030 'pregnant'. Chose H4120 — adverb 'quickly' fits the steward's urgency.
וכתב: Candidates: H3789 'to write', H3790 same, H3791 'a writing', H3792 same. Chose H3789 — imperative 'write'.
textual_notes: This section again interleaves the lost sheep parable conclusion (coming home, calling friends, rejoicing) with the steward parable (the debtor answering 'a hundred measures of oil', being told to write fifty).
חמ<ים appears to be damaged/incomplete text. The < suggests a lacuna or scribal abbreviation. Based on context (reducing a debt from 100 to a round number), this likely reads חמשים 'fifty'.
The ' mark at the end may be a scribal notation or section marker.

verses.literal: And-he-came to his-house rejoicing calling his-friends and-his-neighbors and-said rejoice with-me for I-found the-flock that-was-lost and-he answered-him a-hundred measures oil and-he said to-him take your-document and-do quickly and-write fifty

verses.translation: I say to you: so [or: thus, indeed] there will be joy [or: gladness, celebration] in the heavens over a single sinner making return [or: repentance, turning back] more than over a hundred righteous ones who have no need of repentance [or: returning]

translation_notes: אני (ANI): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the following verb 'say' requires a personal subject, and 'I say to you' is a coherent declaration.
כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'thus there will be joy' produces a natural emphatic statement.

שמחה (SMCHH): Candidates: H8057 'joy/glee', or root מחה H4229 'to erase'. Chose H8057 because the sentence is about joy in the heavens over a sinner's repentance, which is coherent; 'erasing in the heavens' would be forced.
אחד (AChD): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 because 'one sinner' is the natural adjectival reading modifying חוטא.
ממאה (from M + MAH): Candidates: H3967 'a hundred', H3968 'Meah tower', H3969 'a hundred'. Chose H3967 because 'more than a hundred righteous' is contextually coherent.
textual_notes: ב<מים: The text has a damaged/uncertain letter marked with <. The most likely reading is בשמים (in the heavens/skies), but the damaged consonant prevents certainty.

תשובה H8666 is glossed as 'recurrence/reply' in the lexicon but in post-biblical Hebrew carries the well-known sense of 'repentance/returning to God'. The consonants are the same; context strongly supports 'repentance'.

verses.literal: I say to you thus there will be joy in the heavens over one sinner doing repentance more than [over] a hundred righteous ones who are not lacking repentance

verses.translation: Or what [or: which] woman who has ten drachmas and loses one of them will not light the lamp and sweep [or: clean thoroughly] the house and search for it with careful intelligence [or: diligence] until she finds it

translation_notes: אי (AI): Candidates: H335 'where/which', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because 'which this woman' is a natural interrogative construction asking about a hypothetical person.
זו (ZW): Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. Chose H2097 because 'this woman' forms a demonstrative phrase with the following noun.

שיש (ShYSh): Candidates: H7893 'marble', or ש + יש H3426 'who has/there is'. Chose the relative particle ש + H3426 because 'who has ten drachmas' is contextually coherent; 'marble to her ten drachmas' makes no sense.
מהם (MHM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham region', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'them'. Chose H1992 because 'one from them' (partitive) naturally refers back to the drachmas.

הנר (HNR): The candidate given is H5369 'Ner (proper name)'. However the consonants נר also correspond to H5216 'a lamp'. Context clearly demands 'the lamp' — lighting a person named Ner makes no sense.
הבית (HBYT): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house', H1006 'Bajith place', H3487 'object marker'. Chose H1004 because sweeping 'the house' is the natural physical image.

בהשכל (BHShKL): Candidates: H7919 'to be circumspect/intelligent', H7920 same, H7921 'to miscarry/bereave', H7922 'intelligence/success'. Chose H7919/H7922 because 'with diligence/intelligence' describes careful searching; 'with bereavement' would be forced.
עד (AD): Candidates: H5703 'duration', H5704 'until', H5705 same, H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 because 'until she finds it' is the natural temporal conjunction.
textual_notes: א<ה: The text has a damaged consonant. The most likely reading is אשה (woman), fitting the feminine verbs and the narrative context.
תדליק: This verb form (causative/hiphil of דלק) meaning 'kindle/light' is not listed in the provided candidates but is the clear contextual reading from root דלק.
ותכבד: Could derive from כבד 'to be heavy' (in piel: to sweep/clean) or כבד 'to honor'. The context of cleaning a house to find a lost coin strongly supports 'sweep'.

verses.literal: Or which this woman who has to her ten drachmas and she loses one from them will she not light the lamp and sweep the house and search for it with diligence until she finds it

verses.translation: And when she finds the drachma she calls together all her [male] friends and her female friends and her neighbors saying rejoice [or: be glad, celebrate] with me for I have found my drachma — the one that I had lost

translation_notes: וכאשר (VKAShR): Candidates for אשר: H833 'be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happy', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because וכאשר = 'and when', a standard temporal conjunction introducing the next action.
כל (KL): Candidates: H3605 'all/whole', H3606 same Aramaic. Chose H3605 as the standard Hebrew form.
כי (KI): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for/that'. Chose H3588 because 'for I have found' is the natural causal conjunction.

שלי (ShLY): Candidate: H7987 'privacy'. However in context this is clearly the possessive particle של + suffix י = 'mine/my'. The consonants support a possessive reading more naturally than 'privacy' in this sentence about recovering a lost coin.
textual_notes: שלי: The lexicon offers H7987 'privacy', but the consonants של+י function as a possessive pronoun 'mine' in Mishnaic/post-biblical Hebrew. Context strongly favors the possessive reading.
דרכמא/דרכמונים: These are loanwords from Greek (drachma), not native Hebrew, and have no Strong's number.

verses.literal: And when she finds the drachma she calls all her friends and her female friends and her neighbors saying rejoice with me for I have found my drachma the one that I lost

verses.translation: So [or: thus] I say to you: there will be joy [or: gladness, celebration] before the angels of God [or: the Mighty One] over a single sinner who has made repentance [or: returned, turned back]

translation_notes: כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'Thus I say to you' forms a natural concluding formula.
אני (ANI): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship'. Chose H589 for the same reason as section 1.
שמחה (SMCHH): Candidates: H8057 'joy', root מחה H4229 'erase'. Chose H8057 because joy before the angels is the coherent parallel to section 1.

מן (MN): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from God' indicates the source or presence — joy from/of God before the angels.

האל (HAL): Candidates: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H412 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'the God' with the definite article is the natural reading; 'from the not' or 'from these' would be incoherent.
אחד (AChD): Candidates: H258 'unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 because 'one sinner' parallels section 1.
על (AL): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'over/upon', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'over one sinner' indicates the cause/occasion of the joy.
textual_notes: מן האל: Could be parsed as 'from God' (indicating the source of joy) or 'of God' (the angels belonging to God). Both are grammatically possible; the difference is subtle.

verses.literal: Thus I say to you joy will be before the angels from God over one sinner who did repentance

verses.translation: And Yeshua [or: Jeshua] said: a certain man had two sons

translation_notes: וישוע (VYShWA): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as the standard form of the proper name.
אמר (AMR): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same Aramaic, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' naturally follows a named subject.
אדם (ADM): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'a certain man' is the natural start of a parable/narrative.
אחד (AChD): Candidates: H258 'unify', H259 'one/a certain'. Chose H259 because 'a certain man' uses אחד as an indefinite article, a common Hebrew construction.

בנים (BNYM): The candidate given is H1143 'space between two armies'. However the consonants בנים are the standard plural of בן (H1121 'son'). Context clearly demands 'sons'; 'space between armies' makes no sense here.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said a man one there was to him sons two

verses.translation: And the younger [or: smaller] of them said to [his] father: My father, give me the portion [or: allotment, share] of the inheritance that is fitting [or: due] to me. And he divided to them the substance [or: the very essence] of what belonged to him

translation_notes: ואמר (VAMR): Candidates: H559 'say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' is the natural narrative verb here.
קטן (QTN): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan'. Chose H6996 because 'the younger/smaller of them' naturally describes the younger son.
מהם (MHM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'them'. Chose H1992 because 'of them' is the partitive — the smaller of them.
לאב (LAB): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant'. Chose H1 because 'to the father' fits the narrative of a son speaking to his father.

חלק (first): Candidates: H2505 'to apportion', H2506 'allotment/portion', H2507 'Chelek', H2508 'a part', H2509 'smooth', H2510 'Chalak mountain'. Chose H2506 because 'the portion of the inheritance' is a noun referring to a share.
וחלק (second): Same consonants. Chose H2505 (verb 'to divide/apportion') because 'and he divided to them' describes the father's action of distributing his property.
להם (LHM): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'them'. Chose H1992 because 'to them' (the two sons) is the natural indirect object.
מה (MH): Candidates: H4100 'what', H4101 same Aramaic. Chose H4100 because 'the substance of what was to him' means 'what belonged to him'.
תן (TN): The candidate H8565 is 'a sea-serpent/jackal'. However these consonants are clearly the imperative of נתן (H5414 'to give'). Context demands 'give me' — 'sea-serpent to me' is nonsensical.
textual_notes: הירו<ה: Damaged letter. Most likely reading is הירושה (the inheritance), from root ירש (to inherit/possess).
<היה: Damaged first letter. Most likely reading is שהיה (that was/which was), with ש as relative particle + היה.

עצמות: Could be from עצם H6106 'bone/substance/self' (plural construct: the very substance/essence) or עצמה H6109 'might/power'. In context, 'the substance of what was his' = his property/possessions. The word עצמות meaning 'bones' could metaphorically mean 'the very substance/core' of his wealth.

verses.literal: And said the more small of them to the father my father give to me [the] portion of the inheritance fitting to me and he divided to them [the] substance of what was to him

verses.translation: And after a few days, [having] gathered all [his] things, the younger [or: smaller] youth went away on a far [or: distant] road, very [far]. There he squandered [or: lost, wasted] all his inheritance in harlotry [or: sexual immorality, debauchery]

translation_notes: ואחר (VAChR): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because 'and after days few' = 'and after a few days' is a natural temporal phrase.

הנער (HNAR): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5288 'a boy/youth', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because 'the youth/young man' refers to the younger son described in the narrative.
קטן (QTN): Chose H6996 'small/young' as in section 6.
הלך (HLK): Candidates: H1980 'to walk/go', H1981 same, H1982 'journey/wayfarer', H1983 'toll'. Chose H1980 because 'went for himself on a far road' describes the son's departure.
בדרך (BDRK): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road'. Chose H1870 because 'on a road far' naturally describes the journey.
מאד (MAD): Candidates: H3966 'very/vehemently', H108 'fog'. Chose H3966 because 'very far' intensifies the distance.
שם (ShM): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. Chose H8033 because 'there he lost' indicates the location where the squandering happened.
כל (KL): Candidates: H3605 'all', H3606 same. Chose H3605.
בזנות (BZNVT): Candidates: H2184 'adultery/infidelity', H2185 'harlots'. Chose H2184 because 'in harlotry/debauchery' describes the manner of squandering.
textual_notes: ירו<תו: Damaged letter. Most likely ירושתו (his inheritance), from root ירש.
הפסיד: This is a post-biblical Hebrew verb (hiphil of פסד, 'to cause loss/waste'). Not in the classical Strong's lexicon but well attested in Mishnaic Hebrew.

מקובצים: Could be parsed as a passive participle modifying 'all the things' (all the things being gathered) or as a temporal clause 'having gathered all the things'. The latter produces a smoother narrative: after gathering everything, the youth departed.

verses.literal: And after days few gathered all the things the youth the more small went for himself on a road far very there he lost all his inheritance in harlotry

verses.translation: And afterward there was a great famine [or: hunger] in the land, and he found himself in want [or: lacking, destitute]

translation_notes: ואחר (VAChR): Candidates: H309 'loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because 'and after' continues the temporal sequence.
היה (HYH): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'there was a great famine' is the natural existential statement.
רעב (RAB): Candidates: H7456 'to hunger', H7457 'hungry', H7458 'famine/hunger'. Chose H7458 because 'a great famine' uses the noun form.
חסר (ChSR): Candidates: H2637 'to lack', H2638 'lacking/without', H2639 'destitution', H2640 'poverty'. Chose H2638 because 'found himself lacking' uses the adjective describing his state.
textual_notes: עצמו: This is reflexive 'himself' (עצם + pronominal suffix), functioning as the object of מצא. Could also relate to עצם 'bone/substance' but the reflexive meaning is standard in Mishnaic Hebrew.

verses.literal: And after there was a famine great in the land and he found himself lacking

verses.translation: And he began to attach himself [or: draw near] to one of the citizens of that kingdom [or: dominion], and he sent him into his fields [or: his city] to tend [or: guard, keep] the pigs

translation_notes: לקרב (LQRB): Candidates: H7126 'to approach/bring near', H7127 same, H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 same, H7130 'center/midst', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because 'to draw near to one of the citizens' describes seeking help/attachment.
לאחד (LAChD): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 because 'to one of the citizens' is the natural partitive construction.
מלכות (MLKVT): Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth'. Chose H4438 because 'that kingdom' is the coherent political entity.
בעירו (BAYRV): The candidate H5900 'Iru (proper name)' does not fit. The consonants match עיר (H5892 'city') + possessive suffix. 'In his city/fields' describes the location where the pigs were kept.

לשמור (LShMVR): Candidates: H8053 'Shamur (name)', root מור H4171 'to barter'. However the consonants match the infinitive of שמר (H8104 'to guard/keep/tend'). 'To keep the pigs' is the coherent reading.
textual_notes: בעירו: Could be read as 'in his city' (עיר H5892) or 'in his field' — the narrative context suggests rural land/fields, but the consonants most directly read 'his city'. Some Hebrew texts use this to mean the man's estate or domain.
והתחיל: A post-biblical Hebrew verb (hiphil of חלל or denominative). Not in the Strong's classical lexicon but common in Mishnaic Hebrew meaning 'to begin'.

verses.literal: And he began to draw near to one of [the] citizens of that kingdom and he sent him in his city to keep the pigs

verses.translation: And he longed [or: craved] to eat what [or: from what] the pigs were eating, and no one was giving [anything] to him

translation_notes: מה (MH): Candidates: H4100 'what', H4101 same. Chose H4100 because 'what the pigs were eating' is the natural relative/interrogative pronoun used as a relative here.
ואין (VAIN): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because 'and there was no one giving to him' uses אין as the negative existential.
textual_notes: <החזירים: Damaged first letter. Most likely reading is שהחזירים (that the pigs) with ש as relative particle, giving 'what the pigs were eating'. Alternatively could be מהחזירים (from what the pigs [ate]).
נותנין: This is a Mishnaic Hebrew plural participial form (with -ין ending rather than biblical -ים), confirming the post-biblical register of this text.

verses.literal: And he desired to eat what the pigs were eating and no one was giving to him

verses.translation: And he said in his heart: How many hired workers have more than enough food [or: abound in eating] in my father's house, and I am dying here of hunger [or: famine]!

translation_notes: והוא (ה-ו-א): H1931 'he' vs H1933 'to be/exist'. As subject pronoun before a verb of speech, H1931 'he' is the natural reading.
אמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. With בלבו (in his heart) following, this is clearly a verb of speech — H559 'said'.

כמה: Could be H3642 'to pine after' or כ + מה (H4100) 'how many/how much'. In context before שכירים (hired workers), 'how many' makes a coherent exclamatory question; 'to pine after' would need a different syntactic structure.
מרבים: From רבה H7235 'to be/become many, to abound' — participle plural. Fits the sense of workers having abundance.

מת: H4962 lists only 'an adult/man (plural only)'. However, the consonants מת also correspond to the participle of מות H4191 'to die'. With אני (I) preceding, 'I am dying' is the only coherent reading — one does not say 'I am an adult' in the context of starvation.
בכאן: The ב prefix + כאן, a post-biblical Hebrew adverb meaning 'here'. Not fully captured by H575 אן 'where'; this is a compound locative 'in here/in this place'.
ברעב (ר-ע-ב): Candidates: H7456 'to hunger', H7457 'hungry', H7458 'hunger/famine'. After the preposition ב, the noun H7458 'hunger/famine' fits: 'in/of hunger'.
textual_notes: מת: The Strong's candidate provided (H4962) means 'an adult man' and is used only in plural. The consonants however also match the active participle of מות (H4191) 'to die.' The context demands 'dying' — this is likely a gap in the provided candidate list.
בכאן is post-biblical Hebrew (Mishnaic/Medieval), suggesting this manuscript reflects a later Hebrew register.

verses.literal: And he said in his heart how many hired-workers have-abundance in food [of the] house [of] my father and I [am] dying in here in hunger

verses.translation: I will arise and go to my father, and when I come before him I will say to him: I have sinned against the heavens [or: against God] and against you.

translation_notes: ואלך: The candidate H479 'these' does not fit. The consonants א-ל-ך clearly represent the 1cs imperfect of הלך H1980 'to walk/go'. The candidate list appears incomplete.
אל (א-ל): Candidates include H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Before אבי 'my father', the preposition H413 'to' is the natural directional reading.
אמר (א-מ-ר): H559 'to say' — here functioning as 1cs imperfect (cohortative sense), 'I will say', consistent with the future planning context.
אני (א-נ-י): H589 'I' vs H590 'ship/fleet'. Before חטאתי 'I sinned', the pronoun 'I' is the obvious reading.
ל<מים: The damaged letter likely yields לשמים — ל + שמים (H8064) 'heavens'. 'I have sinned to the heavens' = sinned against God/heaven.
textual_notes: ל<מים: A letter is damaged/missing (indicated by <). The most likely reconstruction is לשמים (to the heavens), which parallels the pattern 'sinned against heaven and against you.' Other reconstructions are theoretically possible but contextually implausible.
אמר could be parsed as 1cs perfect ('I said') or imperfect/cohortative ('I will say'). Context of planning future speech favors imperfect.

verses.literal: I will arise and I will go to my father and when I come before him I will say to him I have sinned to the heavens and to you

verses.translation: And already I am not worthy to be called your son. Make [or: treat] me like one of your hired workers.

translation_notes: וכבר (כ-ב-ר): Candidates: H3527 'to plait/augment', H3528 'long ago/already/hitherto', H3529 'Kebar river'. In the context of 'I am no longer worthy,' H3528 'already/hitherto' fits perfectly as a temporal adverb meaning 'already' or 'no longer.'
אחד (א-ח-ד): H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' vs H259 'one/first'. Before משכיריך 'of your hired workers,' the numeral H259 'one' is the clear reading.
textual_notes: ראוי is a post-biblical Hebrew adjective meaning 'worthy/fitting' (from ראה 'to see'), not found in Strong's biblical lexicon. This further confirms the manuscript's later Hebrew register.
איני = אין + suffix 'I' — a negation of existence 'I am not.' Not in the provided candidates but standard Hebrew.

verses.literal: And already I am not worthy to be called your son make for me like one of your hired-workers

verses.translation: And he arose and came to his father. And while [he was] still far from him, the father was filled with compassion [or: deep mercy] for the son, and being with him [or: when he reached him], he embraced him and kissed him.

translation_notes: אל (א-ל): H413 'to/near' — directional preposition before אביו 'his father', same usage as section 2.

ואם: H517 'mother' vs H518 'if/while/when'. Before שעדיין רחוק 'still far,' H518 functioning as 'while/when' creates the coherent image of the father seeing the son while he was still far away. 'Mother' would be syntactically stranded.
הבן: H1894 'ebony' vs H1121 'son' with article ה. In a narrative about a father and son, 'the son' is the obvious reading. 'Ebony' produces nonsense.
האב: H1 'father' vs H3 'green plant'. With the article ה, 'the father' fits the narrative; 'the green plant' is absurd here.
על (ע-ל): H5921 'upon/over/against/for' — used with רחמים 'compassion' to indicate the object of compassion: 'compassion for the son.'

ונ<קו: Damaged letter. The context of embracing and the physical reunion strongly suggests ונשקו from נשק H5401 'to kiss.' The sequence 'embraced him and kissed him' is a natural pairing of reunion gestures.
textual_notes: ואם שעדיין רחוק: The word שעדיין is post-biblical (Mishnaic Hebrew) meaning 'that still/yet.' The conjunction ואם here functions as 'and while/when' rather than 'and if,' though both parsings are grammatically possible.
ונ<קו: A letter is damaged. Most likely ונשקו 'and kissed him' (from נשק H5401). An alternative reconstruction ונחקו is far less plausible contextually.

The syntax 'the son the father was filled with compassion' is unusual — it appears the father saw the son (implied), then the subject shifts to the father. Hebrew narrative sometimes front-loads the object this way.

verses.literal: And he arose and came to his father and while still far from him the son the father was filled [with] compassion over the son and while he [was] with him he embraced him and kissed him

verses.translation: And the son said to him: My father, I have sinned against the heavens [or: against God] and against you, and already I am not worthy to be called your son.

translation_notes: והבן: H1894 'ebony' vs H1121 'son'. Same as section 4 — 'the son' is the only coherent reading in this narrative.
אמר: H559 'to say' — 3ms perfect, 'said', fitting the narrative past tense.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'ship'. Before חטאתי 'I sinned', pronoun 'I' is the clear reading.
וכבר: H3528 'already/hitherto' — same usage as section 3.
להקרא: H7121 'to call' in nifal infinitive 'to be called' vs H7122 'to encounter'. Being 'called your son' (named/designated) fits; 'to be encountered as your son' is forced.
textual_notes: ל<מים: Same damaged letter as section 2. Reconstructed as לשמים 'to the heavens.'

verses.literal: And the son said to him my father I have sinned to the heavens and to you and already I am not worthy to be called your son

verses.translation: And after that, he said to his servants: Go, all of you, bring the first [or: finest] garment, and come and clothe him, and place a ring [or: signet] on his hand, and put shoes on his feet.

translation_notes: ואחרי: The candidate H317 'other' is the adjective אחרי, but the consonants א-ח-ר-י more commonly function as the preposition אחרי (H310) 'after/behind.' Before כן 'so/thus,' the phrase אחרי כן = 'after that/afterwards' is a standard Hebrew expression.
כן: H3651 'so/thus/right' vs H3653 'pedestal' vs H3654 'gnat'. In the phrase אחרי כן, H3651 is standard: 'after thus' = 'after that.'
אמר: H559 'to say' — the father speaking to his servants.
לכו: The candidate H3551 'window' (for כו) does not apply. This is the imperative plural of הלך H1980 'to go' — לכו 'go!'
שאו: The candidate H176 'or/desire' for או does not apply. This is the imperative plural of נשא H5375 'to carry/bring' — שאו 'carry/bring!'

התלמיד: H8527 'a pupil/student'. However, in later Hebrew usage, תלמיד can also refer to a garment/robe (from the root meaning 'to wrap'). The context of clothing someone demands 'garment.' This is a known semantic range issue.
ובאו: Same as שאו — imperative plural of בוא H935 'to come' — 'and come!'
בידו: H3035 'Jiddo' is a proper name. The consonants י-ד-ו with prefix ב clearly read ב + יד + ו = 'on his hand' (from יד H3027).
textual_notes: התלמיד (H8527): Strong's defines this as 'a pupil.' In biblical Hebrew this is extremely rare (only Chron 25:8). In the context of 'bring the ___ the first and clothe him,' a garment is expected. Some medieval Hebrew texts use תלמיד in senses derived from post-biblical usage. This could also be a scribal peculiarity or the manuscript may use a variant term. The narrative logic overwhelmingly demands a garment/robe reading.
שאו could also theoretically be from שוא, but the imperative of נשא H5375 'carry/bring' is the standard parsing and fits the command context perfectly.

verses.literal: And after so he said to his servants go all of you bring the garment the first and come and clothe him and place a ring on his hand and shoe his feet

verses.translation: And bring a fattened calf, and let us eat and let us drink [or: celebrate].

translation_notes: ושאו: Same as section 6 — imperative plural of נשא H5375 with ו conjunction: 'and bring/carry.'
עגל: H5695 'a calf' vs H5696 'circular.' Before שמן 'fat,' 'a calf' produces the coherent image of a fattened calf for slaughter; 'circular fat' is nonsensical.
שמן: H8080 'to be oily/gross', H8081 'grease/oil', H8082 'greasy/fat/rich'. As an adjective modifying עגל 'calf,' H8082 'fat/fattened' is the natural reading — a fattened calf for a feast.

verses.literal: And bring a calf fat and let us eat and let us drink

verses.translation: For this son of mine was dead, and we have found him alive! And he began to eat [or: they began to feast].

translation_notes: כי: H3587 'brand/scar' vs H3588 'for/because/that'. As a conjunction introducing an explanatory clause, H3588 is the clear reading.
זה: H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. Before בני 'my son,' the demonstrative H2088 'this' makes sense: 'this son of mine.' A sheep before 'my son' is nonsensical.
בני: H1137 'Bani (proper name)' vs H1121 בן with 1cs suffix 'my son'. In the narrative context of a father speaking about his child, 'my son' is the obvious reading.
מת: As in section 1, the consonants מת here mean 'dead' (adjective/participle from מות H4191), not H4962 'adult man.'
היה: H1961 'to be/exist/become' vs H1962 'ruin'. With מת preceding, 'was dead' (H1961) produces a coherent past state; 'ruin' is syntactically awkward.
חי: H2416 'alive/living' vs H2417 (Aramaic) 'alive/life'. H2416 fits the Hebrew context: 'found him alive.'
textual_notes: והתחיל is a hitpael form of חלל (H2490 'to begin/profane/pierce'). In hitpael, 'he began' is the standard meaning. This is a later Hebrew verbal usage.
לאכול: The singular 'he began to eat' could refer to the son specifically, or could be a collective reference to the feast beginning. The singular verb form suggests the former.

verses.literal: For this my son dead he was and we found him alive and he began to eat

verses.translation: And the older [or: great] son was in the field, and when he came and drew near to the house, he heard the singing [or: music] and the dances.

translation_notes: והבן: H1121 'son' with article — 'the son,' consistent with previous sections.
היה: H1961 'was/existed' — past state: 'was in the field.'
בשדה: H7704 'field' vs H7705 'wife/mistress.' With ב prefix and the narrative of the elder son being away working, 'in the field' is the coherent image.

נגש: H5065 'to drive/oppress/tax' vs H5066 'to draw near/approach.' Before אל הבית 'to the house,' H5066 'drew near/approached' creates the natural image of someone coming home; 'oppressed toward the house' is nonsensical.
אל: H413 'to/toward' — directional before הבית.
שמע: H8085 'to hear' vs H8088 'something heard/report'. As a verb with objects following (singing and dances), H8085 'he heard' is correct.
ה<יר: Damaged letter. Most likely השיר (from שיר H7892 'song/singing') with article ה. The context of hearing music and dances at a celebration strongly supports this.
הבית: H1004 'house' with article — 'the house.'
textual_notes: ה<יר: Damaged letter, reconstructed as השיר 'the song/singing' (H7892). Could theoretically be other words but the pairing with מחולות 'dances' in a celebration context makes שיר nearly certain.
והמחולות: From מחולה H4246 'a dance/round dance' — plural with article and conjunction. Standard biblical Hebrew word for festive dancing.

verses.literal: And the son the great was in the field and when he came he drew near to the house he heard the singing and the dances

verses.translation: And he called one of the servants and asked him: What is this?

translation_notes: וקרא: H7121 'to call' vs H7122 'to encounter.' He actively summoned a servant — H7121 'called' is the deliberate action; 'encountered' would be accidental, which doesn't fit the purposeful questioning that follows.
אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/first.' Before מן העבדים 'of the servants,' H259 'one' is the clear reading: 'one of the servants.'
מן: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4482 'musical chord.' Between אחד 'one' and העבדים 'the servants,' the partitive preposition H4480 'from/of' is the only coherent choice.
ושאלו: The candidates listed (H431 'lo!', H432 'if/nay') relate to אלו, but the full word is ושאלו — from שאל H7592 'to ask/inquire' with 3ms suffix: 'and asked him.'
מה: H4100 'what?' vs H4101 (Aramaic equivalent). The Hebrew H4100 is appropriate.
זה: H2088 'this' vs H2089 'sheep' vs H2090 'this/that.' After מה 'what,' H2088 gives 'what is this?' — a natural question. 'What sheep?' would be contextually odd when asking about music and dancing.

verses.literal: And he called one from the servants and asked him what [is] this

verses.translation: And I said to him: Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered a great [or: fattened] calf, because he returned to him alive and healthy [or: whole, robust].

translation_notes: עגל (ʿ-g-l): Candidates: H5695 'calf/steer', H5696 'circular'. In context of a father slaughtering something for a feast, 'calf' is the coherent reading. Chose H5695.
אחד (ʾ-ḥ-d): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. As an adjective modifying 'calf' — 'one great calf' — H259 is the natural choice.

בעבור (b-ʿ-b-w-r): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. The prepositional sense 'because/on account of' fits the causal clause explaining why the calf was killed. Chose H5668.
חי (ḥ-y): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)/life'. The Hebrew form H2416 fits this Hebrew text describing the brother's return alive.
ש<ב: The < likely represents a damaged or uncertain letter. The context strongly suggests שב from root שוב (to return), describing the brother coming back.
textual_notes: The consonants ש<ב contain a damaged/uncertain character (<). Context strongly favors שב from שוב (to return), but the original letter is not fully legible.

verses.literal: And I said to him your brother came and your father killed [the] calf one great because he returned to him alive and well

verses.translation: And the older [or: greater] son, when he heard, was enraged exceedingly and was not willing to enter into the house.

translation_notes: והבן (w-h-b-n): Candidates: H1894 'ebony', H1121 'son'. In context of a narrative about a father and sons, 'the son' is the only coherent reading. Chose H1121 with definite article ה.
כעס (k-ʿ-s): Candidates: H3707 'to trouble/grieve/rage/be indignant', H3708 'vexation (noun)'. As the main verb of the clause, the verbal form H3707 fits — he raged/was angry. Chose H3707.

עד (ʿ-d): Candidates include H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'as far as/to the degree of', H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness'. Combined with מאד (exceedingly), the adverbial 'to the degree of' (H5704) makes clear sense.
מאד (m-ʾ-d): Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/exceedingly', H108 'fog' (from root אד). With עד preceding it, 'exceedingly' (H3966) is the natural intensifier.
בבית (b-b-y-t): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 same, H1006 'Bamah place', H3487 'object marker'. A house is the coherent setting for a feast. Chose H1004.
textual_notes: כשומעו and שיכנס appear to be later Hebrew (Mishnaic/Medieval) constructions: כשומעו = 'when he heard' (כ + infinitive + pronominal suffix), שיכנס = 'that he enter' (ש + imperfect of כנס). These forms lack Strong's numbers as they are post-biblical constructions.

verses.literal: And the son the great when he heard was angry unto exceedingly and not was willing that he enter in the house

verses.translation: And he answered him and said my father behold how many years I served you [and] I never transgressed your commandments and you never gave [me] even one goat to eat with my friends [or: loved ones] and Abraham said to him they have Moses and the prophets and let them hear [or: heed] them

translation_notes: ענה (ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to heed/respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to respond', H6033 'to depress', H6034 'Anah (name).' Chose H6030 because 'he answered him' is the standard dialogue introduction.
הנה (הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation.' Chose H2009 because 'behold, how many years' is a natural exclamatory opening.
כמה (כמה/מה): Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what/how.' Chose H4100 because כ+מה = 'how many/how much,' fitting 'how many years.'

שנים (שנים): Candidate: H8147 'two/twofold.' However the consonants שנים also represent the plural of שנה (year) = 'years' (H8141). Context demands 'years' not 'two,' as 'how many two' is incoherent while 'how many years' is natural.

שעיר (שעיר): Candidates: H8163 'shaggy/he-goat', H8164 'a shower', H8165 'Seir (mountain).' Also עיר candidates: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'donkey colt.' Chose H8163 because 'not even one goat to eat' fits the complaint about never receiving a feast animal.
אחד (אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first.' Chose H259 because 'one goat' specifies the minimal amount never given.
עם (עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5972 'a people', H5973 'with', H5974 'with.' Chose H5973 because 'to eat with my friends' is the natural prepositional use.
משה (משה): Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'a debt', H7716 'a sheep/goat.' Chose H4872 because 'Moses and the prophets' is a reference to authoritative teaching.
להם (להם/הם): Chose H1992 — 'to them,' referring to the brothers.
הוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist.' Chose H1931 — 'to them there is' or 'they have' — introducing what the brothers already possess.
textual_notes: This section appears to conflate two distinct narrative voices or scenes: the first part ('my father, behold how many years I served you...') resembles a loyal son's complaint, while the second part ('they have Moses and the prophets') is Abraham's response about the brothers. This may indicate the manuscript weaves together related narrative threads.
ע״בדתיך and אוה״בי contain the abbreviation marker ״ suggesting the scribe abbreviated or marked these words specially. ע״בדתיך = עבדתיך 'I served you'; אוה״בי = אוהבי 'my loved ones/friends.'
שנים: The candidates list only H8147 'two,' but in context this must be the plural of שנה 'year' (H8141). The same consonants support both readings; 'years' is demanded by 'how many.'

verses.literal: And he answered him and said my father behold how many years I served you not I transgressed against your commandments and you not gave ever a goat one to eat it with my friends and Abraham said to him to them he [is] Moses and the prophets and they will hear them

verses.translation: And when your youngest [or: lesser] son came who squandered [or: destroyed] his substance [or: possessions] with harlots you slaughtered for him a fatted calf and he said no Abraham but [or: however] if some of the dead go to them they will repent [or: turn back]

translation_notes: הקטן (קטן): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive/young', H6997 'Katan (name).' Chose H6996 because 'the small/youngest son' fits the narrative of a younger child.
עם (עם): Candidates: H5971 'people', H5972 'people', H5973 'with', H5974 'with.' Chose H5973 because 'with harlots' is the prepositional use.
עגל (עגל): Candidates: H5695 'a calf', H5696 'circular.' Chose H5695 because 'a fatted calf' is a feast animal, coherent with the narrative of celebration.
שמן (שמן): Candidates: H8080 'to be oily/gross', H8081 'oil/grease', H8082 'greasy/fat/rich', H4478-H4482 (various). Chose H8082 because 'fat calf' = a fattened calf prepared for feasting.
אתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you.' Chose H859 because 'you slaughtered' has 'you' as the subject.
אבל (אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet.' Chose H61 because 'but/however' introduces a counter-argument.
אם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if.' Chose H518 because 'if some of the dead go to them' is a conditional statement.
מקצת (קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a portion/end', H7118 'a portion.' Chose H7117 because 'some of/a portion of the dead' specifies a partial group.
להם (להם/הם): Chose H1992 'them' with preposition — 'to them.'
הם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they.' Chose H1992 because 'they will do repentance' has 'they' as subject.
והוא (הוא): Chose H1931 'he' — 'and he said.'
אמר: Chose H559 'to say.'
לא: Chose H3808 'no' — a direct negation/refusal.

תשובה (תשובה): Candidate: H8666 'a recurrence/return/reply.' In later Hebrew this word takes on the meaning 'repentance' (lit. 'returning'). Chose H8666 in its developed sense of repentance/turning back.
textual_notes: וכא״שר contains the abbreviation marker ״, likely representing כאשר 'when/as.' Similarly בע״דו likely represents בעדו 'for him/on his behalf.'
]בא[ is marked with brackets in the source text, indicating the scribe or a later hand marked this word as uncertain, supplied, or restored. The root בוא (to come) fits the context.

עצמותיו: The consonants עצמות+יו could mean 'his bones' (from עצם H6106) or 'his substance/essence/possessions' (from עצם H6108 meaning 'might/substance'). In context, 'squandered his substance/possessions' is the coherent reading.
שהפסיד: This verb root פסד is not classical biblical Hebrew but appears in later/Mishnaic Hebrew meaning 'to destroy/ruin/lose.' This confirms the late provenance of the manuscript.

המתה: This appears to be from the root מות 'to kill/slaughter' in a causative (Hiphil) form — 'you caused to die / you slaughtered.' Alternatively it could be parsed as ה+מתה but the context of preparing a calf for a feast demands a slaughter verb.

This section conflates two narrative threads: the complaint about the prodigal son (first half) and the rich man's plea about the dead visiting the living (second half). The transition at 'and he said no Abraham but...' shifts back to the rich man speaking to Abraham.

verses.literal: And when came your son the small who destroyed his substance with harlots you slaughtered for him a calf fat and he said no Abraham but if some from the dead will go to them they will do repentance

verses.translation: And the man said to him you have been with me always and all that [is] mine [is] yours and Abraham said no if they do not hear [or: heed] Moses and the prophets even if one of the prophets returns alive they will not believe

translation_notes: והאיש (איש): Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly.' Chose H376 because 'and the man said' introduces a speaker.
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' for both occurrences.
אתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you.' Chose H859 because 'you were with me always' has 'you' as subject.
וכל (כל): Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 'all.' Chose H3605 because 'and all that is mine' expresses totality.
הם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they.' Chose H1992 because 'they are [yours]' completes the declaration of shared possessions.
לא (first, after Abraham said): H3808 'no' — a direct refusal.
אם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if.' Chose H518 because 'if they do not hear' is conditional.
משה (משה): Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'debt', H7716 'sheep.' Chose H4872 because 'Moses and the prophets' is the authoritative source reference.
ואם (אם): Chose H518 'if' — 'and even if one of the prophets returns.'
אחד (אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one.' Chose H259 because 'one of the prophets' specifies a single individual.
חי (חי): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive/life.' Chose H2416 because 'returns alive' describes resurrection from death.
textual_notes: This section again appears to weave two narrative threads: the first part ('you have been with me always and all that is mine is yours') sounds like a father speaking to an older son, while the second part ('if they do not hear Moses and the prophets...') is Abraham's response about the brothers. The manuscript seems to present these as a continuous dialogue.
א״שר contains the abbreviation marker, representing אשר 'that/which/who.'

יחזור is from the root חזר 'to return/go back,' which is more common in post-biblical Hebrew than in classical biblical Hebrew (where שוב is preferred). This again confirms the late linguistic character of the text.

The final statement 'even if one of the prophets returns alive they will not believe' presents a stark theological claim about the insufficiency of miraculous signs compared to heeding existing revelation.

verses.literal: And the man said to him you with me you were always and all that to me to you they [are] and Abraham said no if not they hear Moses and the prophets and if one from the prophets returns alive not they will believe

verses.translation: But to eat and to celebrate [or: rejoice] I am not worthy [or: fitting], and to gladden others, for your brother — I regarded him as dead and lost [or: perished], and he has returned to us [...]

translation_notes: ולשמח (שמח): Candidates: H8055 'to brighten up, make blithe/gleesome' (verb, causative sense), H8056 'blithe or gleeful' (adjective). Chose H8055 because the prefix ול- indicates an infinitive construct 'and to make glad', requiring the verbal form; the object א״חרים ('others') confirms a causative/transitive verb — 'to gladden others.'

כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'widely used conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because the word introduces a causal clause explaining why the speaker feels unworthy — 'for/because your brother...' — which is syntactically natural here.

כמת: The only candidate H4962 means 'an adult, a man (full-grown).' However, the consonants כמת more naturally parse as כ (preposition 'as/like') + מת (dead, from the root מות). H4962 (מת as 'men') does not fit the context, which pairs it with ונאבד ('and lost/perished'). The image 'as dead and lost' is coherent; 'as a man and lost' is not. I read this as כ + מת = 'as dead.'
textual_notes: This text appears to be from a non-biblical manuscript (possibly a medieval retelling or paraphrase), as indicated by late/Rabbinic Hebrew forms such as איני (I am not), ראוי (worthy/fitting), and the abbreviation markers (״). The words א״בל, לא2כול, א״חרים, ה״שבתיו, ונא2בד, and ונחזר lack Strong's candidates in the provided data, suggesting they are post-biblical forms or abbreviated. I have translated them from their consonantal roots: אבל (but/however), אכל (eat), אחרים (others), חשב (reckon/regard — ה״שבתיו likely an abbreviation for החשבתיו 'I regarded him'), אבד (perish/be lost), חזר (return — post-biblical form).
The numeral '2' appearing in לא2כול and ונא2בד may be a scribal notation or manuscript marker; I have treated it as non-textual.
The brackets ] [ at the end indicate damaged or missing text in the manuscript.

ה״שבתיו is ambiguous: it could derive from שבת (cease/rest) or חשב (reckon/regard) with abbreviation. I chose חשב because 'I regarded him as dead' is the coherent image in context, whereas 'I caused him to cease' would be an odd self-confession in this speech context.

verses.literal: But to eat and to rejoice I am not worthy, and to make glad others, for your brother I considered him as dead and lost, and he has returned to us [...]
